children: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent of Google and DeepMind, has a new leader in the race to make AI conversations feel faster and smarter.
Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking scored 82.6 on Artificial Analysis' Speech-to-Speech Index, putting it ahead of competing models from OpenAI and xAI.
The improvement becomes clearer on harder tasks.
Gemini's Extended Thinking version scored 68.6% on the Tau Voice benchmark, up from 37.7% for the previous generation.
The standard Gemini 3.8 Live costs 84 cents per hour of input audio, less than half the $1.75 rate of its predecessor. First-response latency also dropped to 1.18 seconds from 2.99 seconds.
But there is an interesting catch.

When actual people listen, Google's older Gemini 3.1 Flash Live still comes out on top in blind testing. The new standard model ranks second, while Extended Thinking trails despite completing more tasks.
Google is showing it can make voice AI cheaper, faster and technically stronger. Now it has to make those improvements feel better to users too.
As voice becomes another battleground for AI assistants, that may be the harder benchmark to win.

title: Google's Gemini 3.8 beats rivals on AI voice and slashes costs
